newsitem.title: UK: BT says to slash call charges for September.
newsitem.headline: BT says to slash call charges for September.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc, which is fighting a telephone call price war against its rivals, said on Monday it would slash the charges of national telephone calls in September.

For residential customers on BT's Weekend Saver package, long-distance calls on Saturdays and Sundays throughout September will cost one pence per minute -- the same price as local calls. This is a 69 percent reduction to the normal 3.3p per minute.
BT also said businesses using its September Saver deal will see price cuts of 10 percent on every local and long-distance UK call between 0700 GMT and 1700 GMT on Mondays to Fridays.
Savings will be credited automatically and shown on itemised bills, the telephone giant said in a statement.
